note: Owned 6+ months → no out-of-state sales-tax/use-tax concern, so the sales-tax question is moot. Every vehicle-title-transfer sales-tax branch is gated on ownership_duration=less-than-6-months, so na-owned-6mo-plus fires no branch (document-list neutral); this auto-resolves the fact so the bot skips the redundant question instead of asking one it just called moot.

A current Florida title means the vehicle is already in the FL title system: it cannot be an out-of-state paper/electronic title (title_is_original_paper=na-fl-title), it was previously titled in Florida (vehicle_origin=within-florida), it needs no VIN verification (vehicle_physically_present=na-fl-title), and there is no out-of-state use-tax window to assess (ownership_duration=6-months-or-more, which cascades to sales_tax=na-owned-6mo-plus). All implied facts fire ZERO branches in vehicle-title-transfer (the paper-status, origin, VIN-verification, and use-tax branches all gate on out-of-state values), so this is document-list neutral and only suppresses redundant FL-title questions. Helps every transfer type (gated on the FL-title fact, not on inheritance).

A vehicle already titled in Florida (within-florida origin) can have no out-of-state sales/use-tax concern. Every sales-tax branch (indices 12-14) is gated on vehicle_origin=us-state, so na-owned-6mo-plus fires no branch (document-list neutral); auto-resolving skips the moot out-of-state sales-tax question. Cascades from the title_is_oos=no-florida rule above.

An inheritance is not a purchase by the heir. (1) No FL use-tax / out-of-state sales-tax event → the purchase-framed 'how long have YOU owned it' question is moot; ownership_duration=6-months-or-more cascades to sales_tax=na (the use-tax branches all require less-than-6-months, so no document branch fires). (2) The deceased can't sign a seller's odometer disclosure (SME-confirmed: tax423), so the odometer question is moot — has_odometer_disclosure=na-inheritance fires no branch, and vehicle_model_year_range (asked only to gate the odometer item) is set to na-odometer-moot so it's skipped too. All three implied values are document-list neutral; the inheritance odometer-removal branch in the tree is a belt-and-suspenders guard in case odometer was answered before transfer_reason.

A standard living-owner sale or gift has no estate/heirship to determine, so auto-resolve both inheritance heirship facts to their N/A sentinels and skip the inheritance questions for non-inheritance transfers.

When a surviving co-owner is already named on the title (commonly a spouse joined by 'or'), the vehicle passes to them directly, so the will/probate question is moot — auto-resolve it and skip the question. This also clears the heirship hard-block, since who-takes-title is established by the survivorship on the title itself.

Title is held electronically by FLHSMV — there is no physical title to inspect for alterations/signatures and nothing to classify as paper/photocopy. Auto-resolve both paper-title questions to na-no-title so the bot stops asking them (sessions 19d716d3/ae0b2879 looped these after the customer said the title was electronic). na-no-title fires no document branch; the electronic-held branch handles the conversion guidance.

Customer does not have the title (lost / destroyed / never received). There is no physical title to inspect or classify, so auto-resolve both paper-title questions to na-no-title and stop asking them (session 19d716d3 looped title-condition ~8 times). The lost-or-none branch adds the duplicate-title application (HSMV 82101) the customer must obtain.

The FL-military hunting/fishing benefit (military-gold-sportsman) applies only to Florida RESIDENTS — the sole hunting-fishing branch using fwc_is_military_eligible is gated on fwc_applicant_residency=resident. For a non-resident the military fact can never change the doc list, and the question text ('Are you a Florida resident currently on active-duty military?') is self-contradictory after they said non-resident. Auto-resolving to 'no' fires no branch (document-list neutral) and skips the dead question.
A first-time CDL application cannot have a prior CDL to expire or an OOS license; CLP is only relevant if one exists.
In-state renewal means no out-of-state license is being transferred.
CLP → CDL upgrade: no prior CDL ever held; no OOS involvement.
A never-held CDL implies no prior exams have been passed for it.
No hazmat endorsement → no TSA background-check fee applies.
US citizens do not need lawful-presence documents.
Someone who isn't a veteran cannot have a VA service-connected disability rating — skip the VA-letter follow-up.
Customer not new to Florida → defaults to Florida native; the LLM can override if they later mention a prior state.
Original placard application → no replacement-reason or police-report follow-up.
Renewal application → no replacement-reason or police-report follow-up.
Lost placard → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Damaged placard → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Defaced placard → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Destroyed placard → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Surrendered placard → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Lost in transit → not stolen, no police-report needed.
Florida resident individual → not a visitor (no ISA / no origin question), not an organization.
Out-of-state individual visitor → not an organization, origin is a US state.
Out-of-country individual visitor → not an organization, origin is foreign.
Organization applicant → not a visitor (no ISA / no origin question).
Permanent placard → the prior-temporary 12-month fee waiver doesn't apply.
